points: Q3 2026 will reveal whether brokerage organic growth is decelerating from the 5% Q4 2025 / 6% full-year 2025 pace, especially after reports suggested a record-revenue Q2 that may have been M&A-heavy.

The print will show if adjusted EBITDAC margin can hold near the 30.8% Q4 2025 level, or if integration costs from 33 2025 mergers and workforce/lease terminations are starting to erode profitability.

With consensus looking for about 23% FY1 EPS growth and 13% FY2 growth, Q3 guidance will test whether that growth is mostly deal-driven; a fading M&A contribution would make the FY2 13% target look stretched.
GSHD and RYAN report Q3 before AJG, and their organic-growth and margin commentary will provide a sector read-through that either validates or undermines the warm-short insurance-broker theme.
The 90-day revenue estimate revision trend is already down 0.63%, so Q3 results will show whether the recent 30-day estimate upgrades are justified or whether estimate cuts resume.
At roughly 20x forward earnings and 38.7x sales, the stock leaves little room for disappointment; Q3 will reveal if the below-theme PEG is a value signal or a value trap as growth normalizes.
If Q3 shows organic growth and margins under pressure, the setup into Q4 2026 and FY2 guidance would shift from a premium-growth story to a multiple-compression story, reinforcing the short case.
watch: Brokerage organic revenue growth below the 5% Q4 2025 / 6% FY2025 pace — supports the short.
Adjusted EBITDAC margin contracting from the 30.8% Q4 2025 level — supports the short.
FY2 EPS growth guidance or consensus moving below 13% — supports the short.
GSHD and RYAN Q3 prints showing weaker organic growth or margin pressure — supports the short.
